verses.text: The two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening. Lot was sitting at the city gate. When he saw them, he got up to meet them and bowed down with his face to the ground.

He said, "My lords, please come to your servant's house. You can wash your feet and spend the night, and then get up early and go on your way." "No," they answered. "We will spend the night in the town square."
But Lot kept begging them, so they went with him into his house. He made a meal for them and baked bread without yeast, and they ate.
Before they had gone to bed, all the men of the city of Sodom, both young and old, came from every part of the city and surrounded the house.
They shouted to Lot, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we can have sex with them."
Lot went outside to meet them and shut the door behind him.
He said, "No, my friends. Please do not do this wicked thing.

Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you, and you can do what you like with them. But do not do anything to these men, because they have come under the protection of my roof."

"Get out of our way," they replied. And they said, "This man came here as a stranger, and now he wants to act as our judge! We will treat you worse than them." They kept pushing hard against Lot and moved forward to break down the door.
But the two men inside reached out, pulled Lot back into the house with them and shut the door.
Then they struck the men at the door of the house with blindness, both young and old, so that they wore themselves out trying to find the door.
The two men said to Lot, "Do you have anyone else here? Sons-in-law, sons or daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of here,
because we are going to destroy this place. The cry to the LORD against its people is so great that he has sent us to destroy it."
So Lot went out and spoke to the men who were going to marry his daughters. He said, "Hurry and get out of this place, because the LORD is about to destroy the city!" But they thought he was joking.
As dawn was breaking, the angels urged Lot, "Hurry! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away when the city is punished."
But Lot was slow to move. So the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters, and led them safely out of the city, because the LORD was being kind to them.
As soon as they had brought them out, one of them said, "Run for your lives! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere in the plain! Run to the mountains, or you will be swept away!"
But Lot said to them, "No, my lords, please!
You have been so kind to your servant, and you have shown me great mercy by saving my life. But I cannot run to the mountains. This disaster will catch up with me, and I will die.
Look, there is a town near enough to run to, and it is small. Let me run there. It is very small, is it not? Then my life will be saved."
He said to him, "Very well, I will grant this request too. I will not destroy the town you are talking about.
But hurry and run there, because I cannot do anything until you reach it." That is why the town was called Zoar, which means "small".
The sun had risen over the land by the time Lot reached Zoar.
Then the LORD rained down burning sulphur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. It came from the LORD out of the sky.
He destroyed those cities and the whole plain, all the people living in the cities, and everything that grew on the land.
But Lot's wife, who was behind him, looked back, and she turned into a pillar of salt.
Early the next morning Abraham got up and went back to the place where he had stood in front of the LORD.
He looked down towards Sodom and Gomorrah and all the land of the plain, and he saw thick smoke rising from the land, like smoke from a furnace.
So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, he remembered Abraham. He brought Lot out of the disaster that destroyed the cities where Lot had lived.
Lot and his two daughters left Zoar and went to live in the mountains, because he was afraid to stay in Zoar. He and his two daughters lived in a cave.
One day the older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is no man anywhere around here to marry us and give us children, as people do all over the world.
Come, let's get our father to drink wine, and then sleep with him, so that we can keep our family line going through our father."
That night they got their father to drink wine, and the older daughter went in and slept with him. He did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

The next day the older daughter said to the younger, "Last night I slept with my father. Let's get him to drink wine again tonight, and you go in and sleep with him, so that we can keep our family line going through our father."
So they got their father to drink wine that night too, and the younger daughter went in and slept with him. Again he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.
So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter had a son, and she named him Moab. He is the ancestor of the Moabites of today.
The younger daughter also had a son, and she named him Ben-Ammi. He is the ancestor of the Ammonites of today.
